score_candidate() now branches structurally on len(groups)==1 before the single-answer unpack, so a multi-group/negligible-spread board returns a SelectionLog instead of ValueError: too many values to unpack. Crash confirmed against the pre-fix version (HEAD:question_selector.py) and gone after. The adversarial sweep also showed the original _EPS gate was doing two unrelated jobs -- guarding float noise and deciding what is worth asking -- and set the second by accident: for a two-way split Gini is ~2x the minority fraction, so spread > 1e-9 rejected only a minority mass below ~5e-10, ~9 orders of magnitude narrower than the state the branch's own message described, with the 1e-9 boundary flipping on rounding. Replaced with _MIN_MINORITY_MASS = 1e-3, stated in belief units (share of live weight behind a differing answer) via a new _minority_mass() helper. Self-check covers three boards -- 1e-12 (abstain), 1e-4 (abstain, and >1e-9 so it proves the gate is not float noise), 0.05 relative (a live long shot that still wins) -- plus the uniform case keeping its own distinct reason string. All 5 mutations killed: reverting the gate to spread > 1e-9, dropping the len(groups)==1 guard, floor at 1.0, floor at 0.0, and min() for max() in _minority_mass.

Closed at both ends. (1) admissibility._grounded() no longer quotes entry.claim into the missing tuple -- it names ids and why each leg failed. The ledger already holds the claim under that id, and every existing consumer (moves.py, chat_core.py, panel.py, admissibility's own self-check) asserts on ids, never on claim text, so nothing was lost; what went away is a checker copying the exact content it just refused into a string downstream code renders. (2) turn._voice_prompt() is now an explicit trust boundary: a checker-downgraded abstain (move==ABSTAIN and missing non-empty, which a directly-requested abstain never is) gets a fixed _BLOCKED_VOICE_REASON instead of turn_log.reason. TurnLog.missing and TurnLog.reason are unchanged, so the audit record keeps everything. Leak reproduced against the pre-fix tree (the refused sentence appeared verbatim in the voice prompt while turn_log.move read abstain) and confirmed gone after. Self-checks: turn.py runs the chapters.py-style leak check on the actual emitted prompt over a blocked reveal, a plain abstain (keeps its own reason), and an admissible reveal (still reaches the voice); admissibility.py asserts across three blocked shapes that missing names the failing leg and carries no claim text. Nine mutations killed, including boundary-removed, boundary-always-fires, boundary-keyed-on-move-alone, boundary-swallows-an-allowed-reveal, and re-adding the claim quote in either admissibility branch -- that last one is caught by turn.py's check as well as admissibility's, so the two ends cover each other. moves.py's docstring records why its 'no route that skips the check' claim needed the repair.

run_turn now downgrades a declined ask to abstain, the same shape moves.choose_move already applies to a reveal admissibility.check() refuses: select_question is the checker for ask, so an ask it declined lands as abstain with a reason saying why (_no_question_worth_asking). Previously the voice call was told 'you chose to ask' with no question attached and the persona invented one -- both the generic turn-burning question question_selector.py's docstring opens by condemning, and a reply the SelectionLog could not account for. The downgraded TurnLog leaves missing empty, which is what narrator-7gj's blocked-reveal boundary keys on, so the two abstain shapes stay distinguishable in the log and the declined ask keeps its own reason. question_log is still returned on a downgraded turn -- every candidate stays scored and logged, which is what makes 'nothing was worth asking' auditable rather than asserted. Verified pre/post against HEAD on the endgame path (board at one live hypothesis: pre-fix logged move=ask and told the voice to ask with chosen=None; post-fix logs abstain and the voice is not told to ask). Self-check covers the declined-ask turn (move, reason, empty missing, rejected candidate's text absent from the voice prompt, full scored log retained) and the single-live-hypothesis endgame explicitly, where every candidate scores 0 by construction. Six mutations killed: downgrade removed, downgrade always fires, downgrade keeps move=ask, downgrade populates missing, downgraded log built but discarded, and TurnOutput reporting the pre-downgrade log. Known ceiling recorded as a ponytail comment: with one live hypothesis every ask lands here, and if the endgame should still ask confirming questions the fix belongs in question_selector (a reason to ask beyond discrimination), not a special case in turn.py.

rule_out() now appends a reweight-kind BoardEvent per survivor whose weight the renormalization actually moved, attributed to the elimination that caused it ('renormalized after ruling out <id>'), mirroring what reweight() already did. Verified pre/post: on a board reweighted to a=0.9/b=0.05/c=0.05 then ruling out a, the pre-fix history replayed to {a:0.0, b:0.05, c:0.05} summing to 0.1 while the board held {a:0.0, b:0.5, c:0.5} summing to 1.0 -- b went from last place to leader with nothing in the record attributing the move. Post-fix the two agree exactly. Self-check adds a replay() that rebuilds the board from the uniform prior and its own history and asserts exact equality of weight and liveness, cross-checking each event's old_weight against the replayed state first so a gap surfaces at the next event on that hypothesis rather than absorbing into the total; it runs over the full existing scenario (2 reweights, 3 eliminations, collapse to one survivor) and over a fresh board where the elimination visibly re-orders the survivors. SCOPE EXTENSION, flagged deliberately: reweight() had the identical hole one line over -- its 'abs(new - old) > 1e-12' guard applied a change and skipped recording it -- so the invariant would still have been false after fixing rule_out alone. Changed to 'new != old', with a self-check case that moves every weight by ~1.1e-13 (a real change the old guard dropped) and one asserting a no-op reweight still writes nothing. chat_core.py's assertion that history[-1] is the rule_out was updated to find the rule_out rather than assume the board stopped moving when it fired; it now also asserts the entries after it name that rule_out. Six of seven mutations killed. The one survivor is rule_out's 'if total > 0' guard, which only matters on a board whose weights have already collapsed to zero -- that state is narrator-7z7's, and its acceptance criteria makes it unreachable, so it is not covered here rather than being covered badly.
